claims.text: Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 1 to 2 minutes; if unsuccessful, a second bolus in 5 to 10 minutes, then an infusion of 3 to 20 mg/minute if no renal insufficiency.
claims.quote: usually magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 1 to 2 minutes. If this treatment is unsuccessful, a second bolus is given in 5 to 10 minutes, and a magnesium infusion of 3 to 20 mg/minute may be started in patients without renal insufficiency

claims.text: Correct electrolyte abnormalities such as hypokalemia.
claims.quote: Electrolyte abnormalities (eg, hypokalemia), which can exacerbate the risk of ventricular arrhythmias, should be corrected.

claims.text: Lidocaine shortens the QT interval and may help, especially for drug-induced torsades.
claims.quote: Lidocaine (a class Ib antiarrhythmic medication) shortens the QT interval and may be effective especially for medication-induced torsades de pointes

claims.text: Raising the heart rate (temporary pacing, IV isoproterenol, or both) shortens the QT interval.
claims.quote: Because increasing the heart rate shortens the QT interval, temporary pacing, IV isoproterenol, or both are often effective.

claims.text: Class Ia, Ic and III antiarrhythmics are avoided.
claims.quote: Class Ia, Ic, and III antiarrhythmics are avoided.
